proposals.evidence: DEDR5159 gives Tamil/Malayalam āṟu river with Tamil oblique āṟṟu-. These survey ārɨ/āru/āttɨ river responses are comparative simple-stem correspondences, retaining the rhotic/geminate and final-vowel transcriptions. Minority lects absent from the article are not presented as literal attestations; inheritance versus local transmission remains reviewable. Longer river-bank and large-river responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
